newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN QUIET TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES MIXED IN QUIET TRADE.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were indicated largely softer in quiet trade on Monday.
"The market is quietish with nothing much happening. The rates seem to be stabilising," one broker said.
NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 23 percent, down from 27 percent indicated last Friday and being sold at 22.5 percent versus 22 percent.
Bankers' acceptance bills were being bought and sold at 22 and 20 percent respectively compared to 24 and 21 percent while call money edged up to 22 percent from 20 percent.
The central Reserve Bank indicated a market surplus of Z$8.4 million, down from Friday's Z$77.8 million surplus.
